players.product: Gemma Power Systems EPC for combined-cycle gas plants serving data-center load (4.1 GW in backlog) plus data-center thermal expansion / energy storage tank fabrication

quarterly_data.signal: Argan estimates that approximately 48% of its remaining unsatisfied performance obligations (RUPO) as of July 31, 2026 will be recognized as revenue during the next 12 months, with substantially all of the remainder recognized within 12 to 24 months thereafter.
quarterly_data.figure: ~48% of RUPO (July 31, 2026) expected in the next 12 months

quarterly_data.signal: The 10-Q states that new power generation development is constrained by a limited number of experienced EPC contractors, equipment supply limitations, interconnection delays and specialized labor availability; lead times for large gas turbines, transformers and other grid equipment have extended meaningfully beyond historical norms as manufacturer order books expanded, and equipment costs have risen accordingly. Argan says its backlog growth over the past year reflects this supply-constrained environment for large-scale power generation construction.

The 10-Q states that in November 2025 Argan was awarded a contract for the fabrication of approximately 2,000 horizontal pressure vessels intended for use in thermal energy storage and chilled water buffer cooling systems at the customer's data center facilities (customer not named). To support this contract and future orders, Argan purchased land in Farmville, North Carolina for construction of an additional fabrication facility, expected to be completed during the third quarter of Fiscal 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 2,000 horizontal pressure vessels for data center thermal energy storage / chilled water buffer cooling; Farmville, North Carolina fabrication facility expected in the third quarter of Fiscal 2027
